title: Hello Loop: 10-minute SDK Quickstart + Habit Experiments (draft)
body:
Purpose
---
Short working draft: a 10-minute "Hello Loop" quickstart aimed at turning first-time SDK friction into a repeatable developer habit. This doc mixes an ultra-compact quickstart, three micro-experiments (A/B style), telemetry presets, and a roll-forward plan for shipping as a sandboxed onboarding flow.

Who this is for
- New developers (internal and external) who need a low-friction first run with Redwood SDKs
- Developer advocates and docs owners who iterate quickstarts
- Product/PMs validating activation metrics

Principles
- First success in 10 minutes: minimal friction, no account config required for local demos (uses ephemeral token).
- Habit loop: cue -> tiny action -> quick feedback -> subtle reward (latency/cost preview).
- Telemetry-first: default lightweight telemetry (opt-out) to measure the loop and improve it.
- Sandbox safety: examples must be harmless (no data exfil, short prompts).

Hello Loop: 10-minute flow (alpha)
1) Get the repo: git clone https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-hello-loop.git
2) Create ephemeral token (dev-only): ./scripts/make-demo-token.sh OR use UI "Try in Playground" token
3) Run the zero-install runner (local node): npx @redwood/sdk-hello-loop run
   - The runner performs: warmup (small prompt), health check, short chat generation, telemetry ping.
4) Open the mini-console (http://localhost:4567) — shows tokens, latency, cost estimate, and a Save snippet button
5) Modify a sample prompt (2 lines) and press Run. Observe streamed output and token breakdown.

Minimal CLI examples (kept tiny for 10m)
- curl: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"model":"rwd-small","prompt":"Hello Loop: show me a haiku about routers"}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $DEMO_TOKEN"
- python: from redwood import RedwoodClient
  client = RedwoodClient(api_key="$DEMO_TOKEN")
  print(client.generate(model="rwd-small", prompt="Hello Loop: summarize this commit in one line"))

Micro-experiments (week-long A/B deploys)
Experiment A: "Minimal Console"
- Single page UI, single CTA: run sample prompt. No guidance.
- Measure: time to first token (t_first), run/success rate, demo retention at 1h.

Experiment B: "Guided Microsteps"
- UI shows 3 tiny tasks with inline tips (edit prompt, toggle streaming, inspect tokens).
- Measure: conversion to second run, number of edits, documentation click-through.

Experiment C: "Telemetry Nudges"
- After first run, show a subtle nudge: "We measured your run — enable richer telemetry to see token-level timing."
- Measure: telemetry opt-in rate, downstream activation.

Telemetry presets (lightweight default)
- heartbeat: boolean (true) — 1 event at session start
- run_summary: {success:boolean, duration_ms: int, model: string} (aggregate; no prompt text)
- token_metrics: boolean (default false) — toggled by user opt-in (only counts tokens/time, not content)
- error_counts: {code, message_hash} (no raw message payloads)
Notes: all telemetry can be turned off via REDWOOD_DEMO_TELEMETRY=false or local config file. Must be opt-out for sensitive org demos where required.

Acceptance metrics (success criteria for MVP)
- 60% of new users complete at least one second run within 24 hours of first run
- t_first <= 3s on typical dev laptop for the local runner (warm start behavior measured)
- Telemetry opt-in >= 10% in Experiment C (bench placeholder)
- < 3 documented friction points surfaced via built-in feedback button in the console

UX and copy skeleton (what to show, wording)
- Landing card: "Hello Loop — <10 minutes to first iterate"
- CTA: "Run the sample — no account needed"
- Success toast: small green bar with a token/latency summary and link: "See how we measured this"

Implementation TODOs (short-term)
- [ ] make-demo-token.sh: restrict to dev envs, rotate every hour (Marcus)
- [ ] local runner: add retry/backoff for ephemeral token (Sofia)
- [ ] mini-console: add telemetry toggle UI, link to privacy doc (Aisha)
- [ ] add smoke tests in CI for t_first under simulated env (Jon)

Risks and mitigations
- Risk: users assume demo token is production-safe -> Mitigate: explicit banner, ephemeral token generator and automatic revocation.
- Risk: telemetry perceived as intrusive -> Mitigate: clear opt-out and privacy-first defaults, sample telemetry page explaining what we collect.
- Risk: expensive token profile during demos -> Mitigate: default to small/quantized model and capped max_tokens=64.

Open questions (notes-to-self)
- Should the default demo use local-mode emulation (no network) for air-gapped customers? Pros: zero-data. Cons: mismatch to hosted performance.
- How do we measure "habit" beyond two runs? Should we instrument week-long retention or Slack invites?
- Do we seed the mini-console with tiny tutorials (3-4 micro-tasks) or keep it purely exploratory?

Rollout plan (phases)
- Alpha (internal): week-long internal dogfood, gather friction log, iterate copy (2 weeks)
- Beta (select customers & advocates): gated rollout via token whitelist + opt-in telemetry (3 weeks)
- Public (playground): auto-ephemeral token via web flow, telemetry on by default but easy toggle (after beta sign-off)

Notes for docs owners (how to keep this fresh)
- Keep the hello-loop repo evergreen with a single canonical sample prompt per quarter (rotate to show new features)
- Add a short changelog entry to console UI when the sample changes (helps AB testing)

Reference snippets (links)
- GitHub PR for runner: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/789 (work-in-progress)
- Linear ticket: INFR-324 (telemetry schema for Hello Loop)

Next steps (this week)
- Prototype local runner improvements (Jon): get t_first reproducible on M1/Intel/AMD
- Draft microcopy and toasts (Aisha): prepare 3 variants for experiment B
- Implement telemetry opt-in nudge (Sofia): backend flagging and UI flow

If you grab this doc for iteration: please leave a 1-2 line note at the top with date + changes. This is intentionally informal — the goal is fast iteration and measurable signal.

-- end of draft --
